'''Martin Charles Raff''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRS|FMedSci|MAE}} (born 15 January 1938)<ref name="cbe">{{cite web |title=New Year's Honours List |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/2009/jan/new-years-honours-list |website=UCL News |accessdate=18 November 2020 |language=en |date=7 January 2009}}</ref> is a Canadian/British biologist and researcher who is an Emeritus Professor at the MRC Laboratory for Molecular Cell Biology (LMCB) at University College London (UCL).<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name=ucl>
{{cite web|title= Martin Raff|work= LMCB - MRC Laboratory for Molecular Cell Biology|url= http://www.ucl.ac.uk/lmcb/research-group/martin-raff|accessdate= 2014-09-20}}</ref><ref name=retired>{{cite Q|Q43203075}}</ref> His research has been in immunology, cell biology, and developmental neurobiology.<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Raff, Prof. Martin Charles | id = U31778 | year = 2007 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U31778 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title= I hated science when I was a child|website=webofstories.com|publisher= Web of Stories|url= http://www.webofstories.com/play/martin.raff/1|first=Martin |last=Raff |year=2014|accessdate= 2014-09-20}}</ref>

==Early life==
Raff was born and educated in Montreal, where he obtained his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1959 and an [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.C.M.]] in 1963, both from McGill University.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=Martin Raff Profile|work=University College London|url=http://www.ucl.ac.uk/lmcb/images/raff/autobiography.pdf|accessdate=2014-09-20|archive-date=2015-07-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150708095328/http://www.ucl.ac.uk/lmcb/images/raff/autobiography.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
Raff was an intern and assistant resident in medicine at the [[Royal Victoria Hospital, Montreal]] (1963–65) and a resident in [[neurology]] at the [[Massachusetts General Hospital]] in Boston (1965–68). He did [[postdoctoral research]] in [[immunology]] with [[Avrion Mitchison]] at the [[National Institute for Medical Research]] in Mill Hill, London (1968–1971), after which he moved to [[University College London]], where he has been since 1971. He served as president of the British Society of Cell Biology (1991–95). He retired from active science in 2002, but he continued to serve on various scientific advisory boards in Europe and America until 2018. After his first retirement, when his grandson was diagnosed with autism, he became interested in the neurobiological basis of autism.<ref name=autism>{{cite Q|Q30494335|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=ucl/> He is co-author of two widely used cell biology textbooks: ''[[Molecular Biology of the Cell (textbook)|Molecular Biology of the Cell]]'' and ''Essential Cell Biology''.<ref>{{Cite book|vauthors=Alberts B, Hopkins, K, Johnson A, Morgan, D, Raff M, Roberts K, Walter P|title= Essential Cell Biology|edition= 5th|publisher= W W Norton|year= 2019|isbn=9780393679533}}</ref>

=== Awards and honours===
Raff has received the following awards for his research:
*1974: Nominated a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO)
*1985: Elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS)<ref name=bio/>
*1988: [[Member of Academia Europaea]] (MAE)
*1989: Feldberg Prize given by [[:de:Feldberg Foundation|Feldberg Foundation]]<ref>{{cite web|title= Prizewinners of the Feldberg Foundation|url= http://www.feldbergfoundation.org/prizewinners/|work=Feldberg Foundation|accessdate= 2014-09-20}}</ref>
*1989: Honorary Member of the American Neurological Society{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}
*1998: Inaugural [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] (FMedSci)<ref name=whoswho/>
*1999: Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}
*2002: Hamdan Award for Medical Research Excellence - Apoptosis in Disease & Health, awarded by Sheikh Hamdan bin Rashid Al Maktoum Award for Medical Sciences, [[United Arab Emirates]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Martin Raff - Sheikh Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Award for Medical Sciences - HMA |url=http://www.hmaward.org.ae/profile.php?id=265 |access-date=2023-04-05 |website=www.hmaward.org.ae}}</ref>
*2003: International [[Member of the National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=nas>{{cite web|title= Member: Martin Raff
|url= https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/martin-c-raff-wu5jiy/|website=nasonline.org|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|access-date= 2014-09-20}}</ref>
*2005: Honorary Degree, McGill University{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}
*2006: The Biochemical Society Award{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}
*2007: Honorary Degree, Vrije Universiteit Brussel{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}
*2010: DART/NYU Biotechnology Achievement Award in Basic Science{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

Raff's son {{ill|Jordan Raff|qid=Q37388121}} is also a scientist.<ref name=jordan>{{cite Q|Q48551849}}</ref><ref name=jwhoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Raff, Prof. Jordan | id = U249549 | year = 2009 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U249549 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref><ref name=whoswho/><ref name=fatherson>{{cite Q|Q50140445}}</ref>
